headline: 115°F heat: Heat wave upends July Fourth celebrations across US
summary: Searing temperatures have forced the cancellation of dozens of parades and concerts as the US prepares to mark its 250th anniversary of independence.
details: A dangerous heat wave has disrupted Independence Day celebrations across the eastern United States, with peak heat indices reaching 115 degrees Fahrenheit (46 degrees Celsius) in some areas.
The National Weather Service warned that numerous daily temperature records are expected to be broken, including consecutive-day and monthly records.
Dozens of parades, concerts, and fireworks displays have been cancelled or postponed across at least seven states due to the extreme heat.

In Washington, DC, the Great American State Fair on the National Mall—a flagship event for the 250th birthday of the US—was temporarily closed on Friday afternoon as temperatures hit 101 degrees Fahrenheit.
Philadelphia's Salute to Independence parade was called off after temperatures reached 103 degrees Fahrenheit on Thursday, tying a record high that had stood since 1901.
Authorities have urged the public to seek shade, drink plenty of water, and remain alert for signs of heat-related illness, warning that the heat wave could become deadly.

headline: Shiba Sanu elected president of Bangladesh Film Artistes Association
summary: Actor Shiba Sanu and Joy Chowdhury have been elected as the new president and general secretary for the 2026–2028 term.
details: Actor Shiba Sanu has been elected president, while actor Joy Chowdhury has been elected general secretary of the Bangladesh Film Artistes Association (BFAA) for the 2026–2028 term.
The results were officially announced at 4:45 am today (July 4) after daylong voting at the Bangladesh Film Development Corporation (BFDC) premises.
A total of 480 out of 573 registered voters cast their ballots. According to the Election Commission, 17 ballots were declared invalid after the count.
In the presidential race, Shiba Sanu secured 243 votes, defeating actor and fight director Arman, who received 173 votes.
For general secretary, Joy Chowdhury won with 237 votes, defeating Rumana Islam Mukti, who garnered 179 votes.
Other winners include DA Tayeb and Elias Cobra as vice-presidents, Subrata as joint general secretary, and Sony Rahman as organising secretary.
Parvez Chowdhury Abir was elected international affairs secretary, Jacky Alamgir as office and publicity secretary, and Maruf Akib as cultural and sports secretary.
Kamruzzaman Kamal was elected treasurer, defeating Jadu Azad. Eleven candidates were also elected as executive members.
The election saw a festive atmosphere at BFDC with two main panels competing: the Arman–Mukti Panel and the Shiba Sanu–Joy Chowdhury Panel.
caption:
Shiba Sanu and Joy Chowdhury take the lead! The new leadership of the Bangladesh Film Artistes Association has been announced.

Actor Shiba Sanu has been elected president, while actor Joy Chowdhury has been elected general secretary of the Bangladesh Film Artistes Association (BFAA) for the 2026–2028 term.

The results were officially announced at 4:45 am today (July 4) after daylong voting at the Bangladesh Film Development Corporation (BFDC) premises.

A total of 480 out of 573 registered voters cast their ballots. According to the Election Commission, 17 ballots were declared invalid after the count.

In the presidential race, Shiba Sanu secured 243 votes, defeating actor and fight director Arman, who received 173 votes.

For general secretary, Joy Chowdhury won with 237 votes, defeating Rumana Islam Mukti, who garnered 179 votes.

Other winners include DA Tayeb and Elias Cobra as vice-presidents, Subrata as joint general secretary, and Sony Rahman as organising secretary.

Parvez Chowdhury Abir was elected international affairs secretary, Jacky Alamgir as office and publicity secretary, and Maruf Akib as cultural and sports secretary.

Kamruzzaman Kamal was elected treasurer, defeating Jadu Azad. Eleven candidates were also elected as executive members.

The election saw a festive atmosphere at BFDC with two main panels competing: the Arman–Mukti Panel and the Shiba Sanu–Joy Chowdhury Panel.
